title: "Nobody is to downvote anyone until I blow this whistle!"
author: DerZim47
selftext:
I posted about my game in a community that makes you fill in an AI disclosure. Four lines: code, graphics, text, sounds. I answered yes four times, because it's true. Also explained my workflow a bit.

The post started well. Good early replies, and not one negative comment the whole time. Then the downvotes came in bursts and buried it, without anybody saying a word. Nobody who did that had played the game. They had read four lines. Gatekeeping with mass-downvotes. No interest in the product. No interest in the person that put in a lot of work.

It was still seen about ten thousand times and it sent people to my Steam page, so it kinda worked. And I'll keep disclosing. I'd rather get buried for the truth than praised for hiding it.

It's not my fault that people conflict using AI with effort and intentions.

  


What has disclosing cost you so far?

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

For context, the game is Tiny Vessel, a companion idle ARPG that lives in a small strip at the edge of your screen. One person, AI in every part of the pipeline, and a lot of hours of manual labour on top of it. I treat agents like my coworkes in what jobs they fulfill. That doesn't make my vision smaller. Nor my dedication.



Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5327220/Tiny\_Vessel/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5327220/Tiny_Vessel/)
